executive_summary: A static security review of the CDF TaskFlow codebase identified severe security vulnerabilities across Supabase Edge Functions, database Access Control Policies (RLS), and React frontend rendering. The overall security risk is CRITICAL. The primary concerns include unauthenticated database mutation and raw SQL injection in Edge Functions, allowing attackers to manipulate or exfiltrate database records without authentication. Additionally, missing authorization checks in Row-Level Security policies allow authenticated users to view all project tasks and escalate their privileges to administrator. Immediate remediation must focus on securing Edge Function endpoints with proper authentication, parameterizing SQL queries, and scoping database UPDATE permissions.
overall_assessment: The application suffers from critical architectural authorization bypasses between the backend Edge Functions and the database layer. Specifically, Edge Functions utilize the Supabase SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY to perform queries, completely bypassing PostgreSQL Row Level Security without implementing compensating authentication or access checks in application logic. This pattern allows unauthenticated clients to read profile data, execute raw SQL injections, and modify arbitrary tasks via mass assignment. Simultaneously, the database RLS policies defined in SQL migrations lack column-level restrictions on sensitive profile attributes like 'role', allowing any authenticated user to elevate their role from 'member' to 'admin'. In the client tier, rendering user-controlled comment text via React's dangerouslySetInnerHTML introduces Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), completing an attack path where XSS can be leveraged alongside insecure API functions.
positive_observations: Row Level Security (RLS) is enabled across all public database tables in the initial schema migration.
Project creation and comment insertion policies correctly verify that author_id and owner_id match the authenticated user's auth.uid().
prioritized_actions: Remove direct usage of SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY in Edge Functions (update-task, get-profile) and replace with user-context Supabase clients that enforce JWT authentication.
Fix SQL injection in search-tasks by replacing raw string template interpolation and sql.unsafe() with postgres.js parameterized query tagged templates.
Implement column-level permissions (REVOKE/GRANT) on public.profiles to prevent standard users from updating their own 'role' column.
Restrict task SELECT RLS policy to only return tasks belonging to projects owned or accessible by auth.uid().
Replace dangerouslySetInnerHTML in TaskComments.tsx with standard React child element rendering to prevent Stored XSS.
limitations: Static source-code review only: no code was executed, and no runtime or penetration testing was performed.
Deployment configuration, infrastructure, and third-party services outside the scanned files were not assessed.
Dependency versions were not checked against vulnerability databases (use npm audit / pip-audit alongside this tool).
Findings marked 'needs validation' depend on runtime context and should be confirmed by a developer.
No automated tool finds every vulnerability; absence of a finding is not proof of security.

findings.title: SQL Injection in Task Search Edge Function
findings.evidence:
const query = `
      SELECT id, title, description, status
      FROM public.tasks
      WHERE title ILIKE '%${searchTerm}%'
      ORDER BY created_at DESC
      LIMIT 25
    `;

    const tasks = await sql.unsafe(query);
findings.description: The search-tasks function constructs a SQL query using string interpolation with the untrusted query parameter 'q' and executes it via sql.unsafe().
findings.impact: An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL statements, allowing them to bypass access controls, extract sensitive data from all database tables, modify database contents, or execute administrative commands.
findings.remediation: Use tagged template literals provided by postgres.js to parameterize SQL queries safely instead of building SQL via string template interpolation and sql.unsafe().
findings.secure_code:
const tasks = await sql`
      SELECT id, title, description, status
      FROM public.tasks
      WHERE title ILIKE ${'%' + searchTerm + '%'}
      ORDER BY created_at DESC
      LIMIT 25
    `;
findings.exploit_scenario: An attacker submits a GET request to /search-tasks?q=test%27%20UNION%20SELECT%20id%2C%20full_name%2C%20role%2C%20bio%20FROM%20public.profiles%20-- to leak user profile details.
findings.review_note: Accurately identifies a critical SQL injection vulnerability in the search-tasks Edge Function where untrusted query parameters are interpolated directly into a SQL string executed via postgres.unsafe().

findings.title: Unauthenticated Task Update with Mass Assignment and Privilege Bypass
findings.description: The update-task function accepts arbitrary JSON updates and applies them using the Supabase Service Role Key without authenticating the requester or verifying task ownership.
findings.impact: Unauthenticated users can update any task in the system and modify privileged attributes such as task owner_id or project_id through mass assignment.
findings.remediation: Pass the client's JWT Authorization header to createClient or create a Supabase client scoped to the user's token. Validate input fields against an allowlist before performing updates.
findings.exploit_scenario: An unauthenticated attacker sends a POST request with body {"taskId": "<target-uuid>", "changes": {"owner_id": "<attacker-uuid>", "title": "Hacked"}} to reassign ownership of any task.
findings.review_note: Accurately identifies an unauthenticated Edge Function endpoint using the privileged Supabase Service Role Key to apply un-sanitized mass assignment updates on any task record.

findings.title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) via Unsanitized Comment Rendering
findings.description: Task comment text is rendered directly into the DOM using React's dangerouslySetInnerHTML attribute without HTML sanitization.
findings.impact: If an attacker inserts HTML or JavaScript payload into a comment, it executes in the browsers of users viewing the task details, potentially stealing session details or performing unauthorized actions.
findings.remediation: Render user-supplied text directly inside React elements instead of dangerouslySetInnerHTML, or sanitize HTML with a library like DOMPurify.
findings.exploit_scenario: An attacker submits a comment containing . When another user views the task comments, the script executes.
findings.review_note: Accurately identifies stored XSS in TaskComments.tsx caused by passing raw comment content to dangerouslySetInnerHTML.

findings.title: Unauthenticated User Profile Lookup via Privileged Service Role Key
findings.description: The get-profile Edge Function uses the service role key to query profiles based on a user-supplied 'userId' query parameter without verifying caller authentication.
findings.impact: Any remote caller can query arbitrary user profile details by manipulating the userId parameter.
findings.remediation: Authenticate callers using their JWT token and enforce authorization checks or rely on user-scoped Supabase client calls.
findings.exploit_scenario: An attacker queries GET /get-profile?userId=<target-user-uuid> to fetch full profile details for any user.
findings.review_note: Accurately identifies an unauthenticated user profile retrieval function using the service role key, bypassing RLS and allowing unrestricted IDOR access to profile data.

findings.title: Privilege Escalation via Unrestricted Column Updates on Profiles RLS Policy
findings.evidence:
CREATE POLICY "Users can update own profile"
ON public.profiles
FOR UPDATE
TO authenticated
USING (id = auth.uid())
WITH CHECK (id = auth.uid());
findings.description: The RLS UPDATE policy on public.profiles allows authenticated users to update their row but does not restrict which columns can be updated. PostgreSQL row-level security policies control row access, not column permissions.
findings.impact: A user with 'member' role can send an UPDATE query targeting their profile row setting role = 'admin' to escalate their privileges.
findings.remediation: Restrict update permissions on sensitive columns using column-level GRANT statements or trigger/CHECK logic in RLS policies.
findings.exploit_scenario: A member executes supabase.from('profiles').update({ role: 'admin' }).eq('id', myUserId) to self-promote to administrator.
findings.review_note: Accurately identifies privilege escalation vulnerability where an RLS UPDATE policy on public.profiles allows users to update any column in their row, including 'role'.

findings.title: Overly Permissive Read Access Policy for Tasks
findings.evidence:
CREATE POLICY "Users can view tasks"
ON public.tasks
FOR SELECT
TO authenticated
USING (true);
findings.description: The RLS policy 'Users can view tasks' uses USING (true), allowing any authenticated user to select all tasks across all projects regardless of project membership.
findings.impact: Users can view private tasks belonging to projects created by other users.
findings.remediation: Restrict task select access to project owners or project collaborators.
findings.secure_code:
CREATE POLICY "Users can view tasks"
ON public.tasks
FOR SELECT
TO authenticated
USING (
  EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM public.projects
    WHERE projects.id = tasks.project_id
    AND projects.owner_id = auth.uid()
  )
);
findings.exploit_scenario: An authenticated user queries the tasks table directly and views confidential tasks created by other users.
findings.review_note: Accurately identifies an overly broad RLS SELECT policy on public.tasks (USING (true)) that exposes tasks across all projects to any authenticated user.

findings.title: Hardcoded Key Pattern Shipped in Client Application Configuration
findings.description: An API key string literal is embedded in the frontend source configuration. Note that the value appears to be a placeholder/demo key, but storing static credentials in client code is an insecure design pattern.
findings.impact: Hardcoded credentials in frontend bundles are exposed to all site visitors and can be extracted easily.
findings.remediation: Inject client-side configuration parameters via environment variables (e.g., import.meta.env) at build time.
findings.exploit_scenario: An attacker inspects the bundled JavaScript file and extracts the hardcoded API key.
findings.review_note: Accurately identifies embedding client-side configuration secret key patterns into frontend source code.

static_signals.title: dangerouslySetInnerHTML renders raw HTML
static_signals.hint: React's escape hatch injects raw HTML. If the value can contain user-controlled content, this is stored/reflected XSS.

static_signals.title: Hardcoded secret-like value
static_signals.hint: A credential-like key is assigned a string literal in source code. Secrets in source end up in version control and, for frontend code, in the shipped JS bundle. The value looks like a placeholder/demo value; report the insecure *pattern* (secret embedded in source/client bundle) without claiming a leaked live credential.

static_signals.hint: A privileged key bypasses database row-level security. Every query made with it must enforce authorization in code (verify caller identity and ownership) or it exposes all rows.

static_signals.title: UPDATE policy on profiles does not protect column(s): role
static_signals.snippet: CREATE POLICY "Users can update own profile"
static_signals.hint: Row-level policies restrict *which rows* can be updated, not *which columns*. If the table has role/ownership columns and no column-level GRANT or trigger protects them, a user can update their own row to escalate privileges or reassign ownership.

static_signals.title: Policy "Users can view task comments" is not scoped to the current user
static_signals.snippet: CREATE POLICY "Users can view task comments"
static_signals.hint: The policy condition never references the requesting user (auth.uid()/JWT claims), so its result is the same for every user. Check whether it effectively grants all rows.
